topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the learning outcomes and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signaling deregulation and pathway mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how extracellular growth signals and intracellular signaling cascades such as Wnt/beta-catenin and RTK pathways are mutated to drive cancer proliferation.

topics.label: Block in terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how impaired terminal differentiation sustains cancer cell proliferation in hematopoietic diseases and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how tumor cells avoid programmed cell death through alterations in p53 and the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance, replicative immortality, and senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address telomere dynamics, TERT reactivation, and p53-mediated stress responses that regulate replicative lifespan and senescence.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and oncometabolite signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the metabolic reprogramming of cancer cells, including aerobic glycolysis, tissue metabolic hardwiring, and the epigenetic impact of oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch and the vascularization mechanisms required to sustain tumor growth beyond diffusion limits.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the systemic invasion, circulatory dissemination, biological inefficiencies, and genomic characteristics of metastatic cancer cells.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding synthesis of cancer hallmarks and closing administrative remarks.
